newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: French soluble coffee market lags ground beans.
newsitem.headline: French soluble coffee market lags ground beans.

text.p: France's soluble coffee market lags behind demand for ground and roasted bean consumption, the general director of Nestle France said here Monday.

Speaking at the International Coffee Week, known in Spanish as Sintercafe, Gerard Le Morhedec said the soluble market only represented about 10 percent of the total volume of coffee drunk in France which he put at 180,000 tonnes per year. He said the figure rose to 15 percent in terms of cups consumed.

Le Morhedec said consumers who only drank solble coffee were a minority 7 percent in France, whereas the majority 51 percent drank both soluble and ground coffee. He said 42 percent were roasted and ground only people.

Nestle, he said, had a 67 percent share of the soluble coffee market in France, followed by Kraft Jacobs Suchard with 23 percent. Private label marketshare, those brands sold by retailers, had the remaining 10 percent, Le Morhedec added.
